title: Clifft: Fast Exact Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits
conversion_notes: Extended Stim templates include T/T_DAG cultivation and distillation; coherent-noise benchmarks use R_Z. No conversion needed; check rotation angle units and postselection conventions.
notes: Paper benchmark repository includes cultivation d=3,5, 85-qubit distillation, and coherent surface code. SymFT benchmark README documents byte-identical vendored cultivation files and explicit provenance. Full escape-stage code is separate. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27058

title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
conversion_notes: The msc, distillation and coherent_surface files use extended Stim gates T, T_DAG, R_X or R_Z. Rotation parameters are half-turns, e.g. R_Z(0.02) = 0.02 pi radians.
notes: The benchmark README identifies checked-in inputs and their provenance. d=3 and d=5 cultivation files are copies of the Clifft paper corpus; d=7 is explicitly an unverified performance proxy, unsuitable for logical-error claims. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28600

title: SOFT: a high-performance simulator for universal fault-tolerant quantum circuits
authors: Li, Zheng, Zhang, Lou, Ying, Liu, Sun
conversion_notes: d=3 and d=5 T/T_DAG cultivation cases in the later SymFT benchmark corpus are usable extended Stim text. Check against original SOFT conventions before treating them as exact replication.
notes: Paper reports d=5 with 42 qubits and 72 T/T-dagger gates and links SOFT repository. SymFT is its successor; the documented d=3/5 files are Clifft-derived, so direct identity to original SOFT input has not been verified. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23037

title: Simulating magic state cultivation with few Clifford terms
conversion_notes: run.py contains T/T_DAG circuit strings; it substitutes S/S_DAG to use Stim noise tooling then restores T/T_DAG before building tsim.Circuit. Extract noisy_injection_str and projection for the d=3 circuit.
notes: Author companion repository specifies paper arXiv ID and implements exact d=3 simulation with bloqade-tsim. The paper also analyzes d=5, but this particular repo advertises d=3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08658

title: Unfolded distillation: very low-cost magic state preparation for biased-noise qubits
conversion_notes: The paper says the simulated X^(1/2) Clifford rotations stand in for X^(1/4); identify the protocol's transversal proxy gates and replace with R_X(+/-0.25) in half-turn units, preserving the original sign and other Clifford rotations. Recheck detectors and output observable.
notes: Paper's data availability links the author code repository; it contains repetition, surface-code, and Toffoli simulations. Exact generator filenames and precise proxy gate positions not yet verified. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41534-026-01197-z

title: Efficient Magic State Cultivation on RP²
conversion_notes: Locate injection and logical verification proxy instructions using t_gadget.py and the paper; substitute the intended T-state injection and controlled-HXY construction, rather than replacing every S indiscriminately. Exact gate mapping remains to be verified.
notes: Repository identifies Stim circuits in circuit_garage and d=3/d=5 cultivation and end-to-end sampling scripts. Paper discusses T injection and verification; proxy-to-native conversion has not been checked. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18657

title: Efficient Magic State Cultivation on the Surface Code
conversion_notes: Repository reports Stim/Sinter Clifford simulation and full state-vector simulation; identify and replace the injection and verification proxies using the non-Clifford protocol and state-vector implementation. The specific replacement sites were not checked.
notes: Author repository explicitly identifies its paper and provides surface-code cultivation circuit generation. The precise compatibility of generated circuits and non-Clifford conversion is unverified. https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01743
